acs.text_first_line: A non-engine writer can place a case
It is off until a consumer exists
A caller that is not approved is refused
A case already in the queue
A case with an open deviation stays with its handler
Two placements at the same time
A case that already has an owner

gap_rows.title: rwb-integration queue-write adapter: the operation owner, the login, the consumed contract field names and the replay window are not fixed by one source
gap_rows.source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 036 Queue write interface for models and agents v1.md; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api POST /queues/{queueId}/placements; tables recovery_case, queue, assignment); Recovery Workbench TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 16, 20 and 41
gap_rows.section: Legacy §3, §4, §10, §12 and §13; Ownership Map api and tables; TSD P2 v3 T3.1; Architecture v5 slides 14, 16, 20 and 41
gap_rows.description: The P2 story of legacy RWB-E2-036 builds an adapter whose operation, login, consumed contracts and replay window no single source fixes. (1) Ownership: the legacy story places POST /api/recovery/v1/queues/{queueId}/placements in the P2 module and its §13 puts the code in recovery/casewf/placement, while the Ownership Map keeps POST /queues/{queueId}/placements with P3 rwb-case, and the WP B-P2-02 assigns the story to rwb-integration. (2) Login: DP-02 gives one login per service and Arch v5 slide 41 gives the schema rwb_integration, but no source names the login literal. (3) Field names: the legacy §12 gives the PlacementRequest elements (caseId, reason, modelOrAgent, version) and the P3 contract gives caseId and reason only; no source gives the JSON element names of the rwb-case placement contract, of the rwb-case parameters contract that carries the approved callers list, or of the rwb-access authorise contract. (4) Status: the legacy AC1 expects 201, while RWB-P3-E1019-CON documents 202 for the P3 placement operation. (5) Replay: TSD P2 v3 T3.1 gives an idempotency_key table with a 24-hour retention and the columns id, idempotency_key, endpoint, request_hash and response, and the legacy §12 gives one placement per case and queue with 409 MSG-P2-024 on a repeat; no source fixes the replay window of the adapter or the column names of the decision_record library table beyond the standard record columns. (6) The admission decision code is D6 in the legacy AC3, which is also the code of the route decision D6 in the Drools design; the placement code is kept as the legacy has it. (7) Path: the caller-facing path on the integration base is named by no source; the legacy story serves the path on the monolith base and the naming rule replaces that base with /api/recovery/integration/v1, so the adapter serves the same suffix with no colon segment and no verb. (8) The message texts are the legacy texts and are copied unchanged.
gap_rows.evidence: Legacy §4 step 1 and §13 (P2 module, package recovery/casewf/placement, POST /api/recovery/v1/queues/{queueId}/placements); Ownership Map api POST /queues/{queueId}/placements owner P3 and tables recovery_case, queue and assignment owner P3; WP B-P2-02 story line RWB-P2-E2036-APP; Architecture v5 slide 41 (rwb-integration schema rwb_integration, rwb-case owns queues, tasks, allocation); TSD P2 v3 T3.1 idempotency_key kept 24 hours; legacy AC1 (201); RWB-P3-E1019-CON 12.1 (202 Placement); legacy §12 Idempotency row; legacy AC3 decision code D6
gap_rows.area: Integration contract ownership and field detail
gap_rows.proposed: Reconcile rather than duplicate: rwb-case keeps POST /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/placements and its behaviour, and rwb-integration serves the caller-facing admission and forwarding operation POST /api/recovery/integration/v1/queues/{queueId}/placements on its own base, which forwards to the P3 operation with the four legacy fields plus the caller service identity and returns the P3 status and body unchanged; read the approved callers list through the rwb-case reference-data and parameter contract under the legacy key rwb.casewf.placement.approved-callers; hold the stored answer in idempotency_key for 24 hours per endpoint and key with the TSD P2 v3 column set; write the admission decision record through the local decision-record library with decision code D6; take the login name from the rwb-integration DB story. The Ownership Map and the P3 contract are the authority for the P3 operation; this row records that the P2 story adds an operation on the integration base and does not take the P3 one.

asm_rows.text: The rwb-integration adapter runs under one database login for the service, read as rwb_integration, the login that owns the rwb_integration schema on the ACE PostgreSQL server.
asm_rows.why: DP-02 gives one login per service and Arch v5 slide 41 gives the schema rwb_integration, but no source names the login literal; the behaviour does not depend on the name and the chart carries it as a secret reference.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 slides 20 and 41 (one schema and one login per service, schema rwb_integration); plan DP-02; Template and Rules §R4
asm_rows.confirm: ACE DBA and the solution architect at the rwb-integration DB story
asm_rows.impact: None on the behaviour; the login name and its grants are fixed by the DB story and the deployment chart

asm_rows.text: The adapter forwards caseId, reason, modelOrAgent and version to the rwb-case placement contract and adds the caller service identity; the JSON element names are those four legacy names in camel case and the response is the placement result returned unchanged.
asm_rows.why: The legacy §12 gives the four PlacementRequest elements and RWB-P3-E1019-CON gives caseId and reason only; no source gives the full request or response element names of the rwb-case placement contract.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-036 §12 (PlacementRequest: caseId, reason, modelOrAgent, version); RWB-P3-E1019-CON 12.1 (body caseId, reason; 202 Placement); Architecture v5 slide 14 (rwb-case owns queues and allocation)
asm_rows.confirm: rwb-case owner at RWB-P3-E1019-CON and RWB-P3-E2036-APP
asm_rows.impact: The adapter body is a superset of the published P3 body until the P3 owner publishes the two extra elements; a field name change is a contract change, not a code change

asm_rows.text: The approved callers list is one configured row of the rwb-case reference-data and parameter contract under the key rwb.casewf.placement.approved-callers, and the row carries the caller code, the caller type MODEL or AGENT, the service identity and the approval state.
asm_rows.why: The legacy story names the configuration key, gives the caller type values and the empty list at go-live, and names no row field; the reference-data default ruling puts the row in rwb-case (DP-07) and rwb-integration holds no copy.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-036 §3 (key rwb.casewf.placement.approved-callers; type MODEL or AGENT; list empty at go-live) and BR1; plan DP-07 and R-PREC default ruling (reference data to P3)
asm_rows.confirm: rwb-case owner and RW-RISK when the first caller entry is loaded
asm_rows.impact: A missing row field blocks the caller admission check; the adapter reads the row as data and fails closed when it cannot

asm_rows.text: The rwb-access authorise answer carries whether the right is held, the capability area and right code, and the permission matrix version that answered; the adapter caches the answer per workload identity for the session.
asm_rows.why: Arch v5 slide 14 gives POST /authorise as the rwb-access operation and the legacy BR2 gives Queue and allocation C, but no source gives the answer elements of that contract.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 slide 14 (rwb-access IN POST /authorise, GET /me/permissions); legacy RWB-E2-036 BR2 and DT11 (matrix version changed before the first caller is switched on); RWB-P4-E1037-CON
asm_rows.impact: The adapter denies by default when the answer cannot be read; the cached answer is bounded by the session, not by the adapter

asm_rows.text: The local decision_record library table carries the standard record columns plus the decision code, the final call, the actions and the actor reference, as the legacy decision_log_entry fields DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 do.
asm_rows.why: Arch v5 slide 20 places decision_record in every service schema and DP-03 owns the library, but the column set of the library table is not stated by any source; the legacy decision log fields are the only named set.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 slide 20 (own schema: business tables + outbox + inbox + decision_record); plan DP-03; LDM v8 decision_log_entry DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018; RWB-P3-E2006-APP §11 (same library use)
asm_rows.impact: The admission record is written through the library, so a column rename is a library change and not an adapter change

asm_rows.text: The 401 of the adapter carries the platform session message MSG-P4-001, whose text is not in the legacy story and is not restated here.
asm_rows.why: The legacy §12 lists 401 MSG-P4-001 and gives no text; the platform catalogue owns the wording and the other stories of this run use the same identifier.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-036 §12 (401 MSG-P4-001); RWB-P3-E2016-CON and the rwb-access stories (same identifier)
asm_rows.impact: Documentation only; the text arrives with the platform catalogue

asm_rows.text: REQ-ACA-010 sits with the access requirements of Program BRD and is met here by the Queue and allocation C check through the rwb-access contract; the legacy story cites the requirement without naming its BRD section.
asm_rows.why: The legacy BR2 cites REQ-ACA-010 and CTL-09 and gives no BRD section, and no file read for this story carries the requirement text.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-036 §8 BR2 (REQ-CWC-018; REQ-ACA-010; CTL-09); NFR-051 (agents run under service identities and are subject to the same role checks)
asm_rows.confirm: business analyst at the Program BRD review
asm_rows.impact: Traceability only; the requirement is satisfied by the same check either way
